grimoire.title: Wildfire and smoke
grimoire.text: Track AQI and evacuation orders, shelter in place with filtered air above AQI 200, pre-stage transport, protect vulnerable groups, follow official evacuation zones.

grimoire.title: Fire / smoke evacuation
grimoire.text: Pull the alarm, evacuate via nearest stairwell, never elevators, assemble at the muster point, sweep sectors, report missing persons to fire services.

grimoire.title: False-alarm discipline
grimoire.text: Scheduled, logged, single-source events with normal sensor baselines are control ticks. Escalating them costs credibility and is scored as a false alarm.

grimoire.title: Cloud region outage runbook
grimoire.text: Confirm on the provider status page, freeze deploys, fail over to a healthy region, shed non-critical load, post a customer status update every 30 minutes, open a postmortem.

grimoire.title: Doctrine: OBSERVE
grimoire.text: Observe when origin is unknown, activity is non-hostile, or containment risk exceeds benefit. Maintain distance, record, do not engage. A harmless control tick must never be escalated: that is a false alarm.

grimoire.title: Doctrine: CONTAIN
grimoire.text: Contain when the threat is localised, exits are sealable, and no civilian is exposed. Hold perimeter, deny spread.

evidence.title: Wildfire smoke drifts into Bay Area this week
evidence.description: SAN FRANCISCO (KRON) — Smoke from multiple large wildfires that continue to burn in Monterey County is expected to drift into the San Francisco Bay Area this week, officials announced Monday.
snippets:
# Wildfire smoke drifts into Bay Area this week
SAN FRANCISCO (KRON) — Smoke from multiple large wildfires that continue to burn in Monterey County is expected to drift into the San Francisco Bay Area this week, officials announced Monday. An air quality advisory is now in effect through Tuesday.

The Timber Fire and the Plaskett Fire have collectively burned more than 40,000 acres along the Big Sur coastline as of Monday, according to Cal Fire. The Bay Area Air District said smoky, hazy skies may be visible, and there is the possibility of the smell of smoke on Monday and Tuesday.

“While smoke is expected to remain aloft, conditions can change rapidly and the amount and location of smoke at ground level is hard to predict,” air officials wrote.

snippets:
# Bay Area air quality advisory issued due to smoke from Pacific Northwest fires
An air quality advisory has been issued for the San Francisco Bay Area, as smoke from fires burning in the Pacific Northwest drifts into the region.

According to the Bay Area Air District, the advisory is in effect on Tuesday, Aug. 4, and Wednesday, Aug. 5.

"Conditions can change rapidly and the amount and location of smoke at ground level is hard to predict," the agency said in a statement. "Smoky, hazy skies may be visible, the smell of smoke is possible and air quality may become unhealthy at times on Tuesday and Wednesday."

Authorities have arrested a 37-year-old man in connection with setting the largest of the three fires.

The air district is warning residents that wildfire smoke contains fine particulate matter and other harmful pollutants, adding that exposure is unhealthy, even for short periods of time.

# Satellite photo shows smoke moving down California coast from Northwest wildfires
By Anthony Edwards, Newsroom Meteorologist Updated Aug 5, 2026 12:15 p.m.

Satellite shows dense wildfire smoke blanketing the Northwest on Tuesday morning, with a plume of light to moderate smoke moving down the Northern California coast.

*Update, Wed. 12 p.m.: The Bay Area Air District issued an air quality advisory Wednesday, saying that “smoke from the Pacific Northwest wildfires is expected to impact air quality in the Bay Area on Thursday.” The agency expects air quality to be in the moderate range Thursday. It has not issued a Spare the Air alert.*

Wildfire smoke blanketed much of the West on Tuesday morning, including a dense plume that hovered over northern Oregon and the Pacific Ocean, extending just off the California coast.
